   `reference/materials/general-measurement.md` and, for magnets, `magnetic-raman-general.md`. They hold how the
   spectrum changes with thickness, strain, doping, defects, temperature, laser and substrate, the quality
   indicators, the known pitfalls and the questions to ask, each with its source. Interpretation without them is
   guesswork from memory.
1. **Conditions first.** Note laser wavelength, temperature, substrate, polarization geometry, resolution. Many

2. **Quality check.** `rl_qc.py`. Spikes are artifacts, never peaks (`reference/artifacts.md`).
3. **Fit.** `rl_fit.py`, then look at `fit.png`. Check weak shoulders and close doublets (2LA(M) next to E2g in

   candidate) and curated literature tables. Do not stop at the top score: check that the strong predicted modes

- One spectrum rarely fixes layer number alone; name the observable and its threshold.
- Laser heating, strain and doping shift lines by similar amounts; check calibration before reading 1 to 2 cm-1.
- Intensity ratios depend on substrate interference and laser energy; absolute intensity is not layer number.
- Resonant excitation changes relative intensities and activates second-order bands; check the laser against the
  material's excitons before calling a band unexpected.
- When something looks odd, say what it looks like and what would distinguish the explanations.

# CrSBr: expert Raman notes

Numbers are as printed in the cited source unless marked "(fig)" (read from a plot, about +-1 cm-1). Locators
"p." for arXiv PDFs are arXiv page numbers; "journal p." = page of the published journal PDF.
Not used here by design: Wdowik et al. 2025 (arXiv 2503.15298) and Sahu et al. 2025 (arXiv 2502.01794), which sit
behind held-out evaluation data.

## Structure, magnetism, irreps
- Orthorhombic Pmmn (D2h), 6 atoms per primitive cell, 15 optical + 3 acoustic modes (Pawbake et al. 2023, PRB 107,
  075421, arXiv 2211.12939, p.3). Gamma = 3Ag + 2B1u + 3B2g + 2B2u + 3B3g + 2B3u; Ag, B2g, B3g Raman active
  (Torres et al. 2022, arXiv 2212.01754, p.2, Eq. 1).
- In normal-incidence backscattering (light along c) only the three Ag modes are expected; B2g and B3g have
  off-diagonal xz / yz tensors and stay weak (Torres 2022, p.2, Eq. 2; consensus).
- Magnetism: intralayer FM with spins along b (easy axis), A-type interlayer AFM below T_N; intermediate phase (iFM)
  between T_N and T_C (Pawbake 2023, p.1). Reported values differ slightly by source: T_C = 160 K, T_N = 134 K
  (Torres 2022, p.8); T_C about 165 K, T_N about 132 K (Markina et al. 2026, npj Quantum Mater. 11, 11,
  doi:10.1038/s41535-026-00850-2, journal p.3). A low-temperature phase near T* about 40 K is DISPUTED: reported by
  Pawbake 2023 (p.2, p.4) and others, absent in high-quality crystals per Uykur et al. 2024 (arXiv 2405.07853, p.1).
- Easy (b), intermediate (a) and hard (c) axes; exfoliated flakes are rectangular with the long edge along a
  (Mondal et al. 2025, npj 2D Mater., arXiv 2410.22164, p.1; Torres 2022, p.2).

## Signature at room temperature
- Ag1, Ag2, Ag3: 114, 244, 344 cm-1 (4L, 2.33 and 1.96 eV, Mondal 2025, p.2); 117, 257, 345 cm-1 (bulk, 633 nm,
  Pawbake 2023, p.3); 115, 245.5, 344 cm-1 (bulk, 2.33 eV, Klein et al. 2023, ACS Nano 17, 5316,
  doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c07316, journal p.5, Fig. 3). Note the Ag2 spread (244 to 257) between sources; treat Ag2
  position with the source's calibration in mind.
- B2g at 92, 194, 301 cm-1 appear only with the sample tilted 60 deg to the beam (Pawbake 2023, p.3, Fig. 1c).
- Atomic character: Ag1 and Ag2 carry Br motion and mediate interlayer coupling; Ag3 is mostly intralayer
  (Torres 2022, p.2, Fig. 1e).

## Thickness
- Ag1 and Ag2 redshift as layer number decreases, Ag3 is nearly layer independent (Torres 2022, p.3, Fig. 1h,
  resonant 1.58 eV). From Fig. 1h (fig): Ag1 about 107 cm-1 in 1L versus about 113 in bulk; Ag3 near 344 for all N.
  Ye et al. 2022 (ACS Nano 16, 11876, doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c01151, journal p.6) also report a gradual downshift with
  decreasing N. Consensus on direction; exact per-layer values vary with laser and substrate.
- Polarization behaviour of all three Ag modes is the same from about 3.5 to 62 nm (Mondal 2025, p.4-5, Fig. 4);
  for thick flakes (62 nm) thin-film interference changes the Ag2/Ag3 intensity ratio (Mondal 2025, p.4-5).
- Layer number is better taken from optical contrast or AFM than from Raman shifts (Ye 2022, journal p.5).

## Polarization relative to crystal axes
- Ag1 and Ag3 are maximal for E parallel to b at all tested energies (1.96 to 2.33 eV) (Mondal 2025, p.3-4).
- Ag2 switches by 90 deg with laser energy: maximal along a at 2.33 and 2.25 eV, near isotropic at 2.06 eV, along b
  at 1.96 eV, back along a at 1.58 eV (Mondal 2025, p.3-4, Fig. 3; Klein 2023, journal p.5, Fig. 3d-f).
- Fits need a complex Raman tensor (relative phase phi_ab between R_xx and R_yy), otherwise four-lobed Ag2 patterns
  (2.25 eV) cannot be reproduced (Mondal 2025, p.6, Eq. 2).
- PL at 1.31 eV (300 K) is stronger along b; it is an independent axis check (Mondal 2025, p.2, Fig. 1d-e).

## Excitation energy and lineshape
- Near-gap excitation (1.58 eV) gives non-Lorentzian Ag modes, extra resonant peaks polarized along b, and a Fano
  (BWF) Ag2 for E parallel to b with 1/q = -0.24; along a Ag2 is Lorentzian (Klein 2023, journal p.5-6; Torres 2022,
  p.3, Fig. 1f).
- Second-order bands (370 to 780 cm-1, widths 20 to 30 cm-1) appear below about 160 K with 1.96 eV excitation,
  growing on cooling; attributed partly to resonance with the B exciton at 1.82 eV (Pawbake 2023, p.5, Fig. 5).

## Temperature and magnetic order
- Ag3 hardens on cooling, is nearly flat between T_C and T_N, hardens again, then jumps at about 25 K; its FWHM
  shows an inflection near 140 K (Pawbake 2023, p.4, Fig. 3; bulk, 633 nm).
- Intensities of most modes rise in the iFM window 130 to 160 K (Pawbake 2023, p.4).
- Zone folding along c below T_N: a B3g mode at 57 cm-1 (Z point) appears below about 130 K while the 71 cm-1 B3g
  (Gamma, seen below 260 K) disappears; a mode near 194 cm-1 grows near T_C; tilted geometry needed (Pawbake 2023,
  p.4-5, Fig. 4a).
- Sharp 467 cm-1 peak (FWHM 2 cm-1) only below about 40 K, origin unresolved (Pawbake 2023, p.5).
- Thin flakes (3L, 1.58 eV): Ag1 intensity rises strongly below T_C and saturates at T_N; frequencies stay constant
  below T_N, unlike anharmonic behaviour (Torres 2022, p.8).
- Polarization b/a ratios change near T_N under 1.96 eV for 5 to 76 nm flakes (Ag1 step-like); the authors argue the
  spin-phonon effect is indirect, via exciton resonances (Markina 2026, journal p.4, p.6, Fig. 2). Interpretation
  not yet independently confirmed.
- Infrared (not Raman): a magnetic mode near 360 cm-1 below T_N and splitting of the 180 cm-1 a-axis phonon
  (Uykur 2024, arXiv 2405.07853, p.3-4). Do not assign a 360 cm-1 Raman feature to it without polarization and T data.

## Magnetic field
- Bulk, 5 K, field 30 deg from c: the 57 cm-1 AFM mode fades and the 71 cm-1 mode returns above about 0.8 T, and
  B2g near 305 cm-1 gains intensity; saturation field from magneto-PL 0.75 T in that geometry (Pawbake 2023, p.5,
  Fig. 4b-d). The critical field depends on field direction and layer number (odd/even effect, Ye 2022, journal p.11,
  Fig. 3).

## Defects, degradation, quality
- D1: shoulder 5 to 10 cm-1 below Ag1, surface related, grows with air or water exposure, strongest in thin flakes

# CrSBr: expert Raman notes

Numbers are as printed in the cited source unless marked "(fig)" (read from a plot, about +-1 cm-1). Locators
"p." for arXiv PDFs are arXiv page numbers; "journal p." = page of the published journal PDF.
Not used here by design: Wdowik et al. 2025 (arXiv 2503.15298) and Sahu et al. 2025 (arXiv 2502.01794), which sit
behind held-out evaluation data.

## Structure, magnetism, irreps
- Orthorhombic Pmmn (D2h), 6 atoms per primitive cell, 15 optical + 3 acoustic modes (Pawbake et al. 2023, PRB 107,
  075421, arXiv 2211.12939, p.3). Gamma = 3Ag + 2B1u + 3B2g + 2B2u + 3B3g + 2B3u; Ag, B2g, B3g Raman active
  (Torres et al. 2022, arXiv 2212.01754, p.2, Eq. 1).
- In normal-incidence backscattering (light along c) only the three Ag modes are expected; B2g and B3g have
  off-diagonal xz / yz tensors and stay weak (Torres 2022, p.2, Eq. 2; consensus).
- Magnetism: intralayer FM with spins along b (easy axis), A-type interlayer AFM below T_N; intermediate phase (iFM)
  between T_N and T_C (Pawbake 2023, p.1). Reported values differ slightly by source: T_C = 160 K, T_N = 134 K
  (Torres 2022, p.8); T_C about 165 K, T_N about 132 K (Markina et al. 2026, npj Quantum Mater. 11, 11,
  doi:10.1038/s41535-026-00850-2, journal p.3). A low-temperature phase near T* about 40 K is DISPUTED: reported by
  Pawbake 2023 (p.2, p.4) and others, absent in high-quality crystals per Uykur et al. 2024 (arXiv 2405.07853, p.1).
- Easy (b), intermediate (a) and hard (c) axes; exfoliated flakes are rectangular with the long edge along a
  (Mondal et al. 2025, npj 2D Mater., arXiv 2410.22164, p.1; Torres 2022, p.2).

## Signature at room temperature
- Ag1, Ag2, Ag3: 114, 244, 344 cm-1 (4L, 2.33 and 1.96 eV, Mondal 2025, p.2); 117, 257, 345 cm-1 (bulk, 633 nm,
  Pawbake 2023, p.3); 115, 245.5, 344 cm-1 (bulk, 2.33 eV, Klein et al. 2023, ACS Nano 17, 5316,
  doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c07316, journal p.5, Fig. 3). Note the Ag2 spread (244 to 257) between sources; treat Ag2
  position with the source's calibration in mind.
- B2g at 92, 194, 301 cm-1 appear only with the sample tilted 60 deg to the beam (Pawbake 2023, p.3, Fig. 1c).
- Atomic character: Ag1 and Ag2 carry Br motion and mediate interlayer coupling; Ag3 is mostly intralayer
  (Torres 2022, p.2, Fig. 1e).

  resonant 1.58 eV). From Fig. 1h (fig): Ag1 about 107 cm-1 in 1L versus about 113 in bulk; Ag3 near 344 for all N.
  Ye et al. 2022 (ACS Nano 16, 11876, doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c01151, journal p.6) also report a gradual downshift with
  decreasing N. Consensus on direction; exact per-layer values vary with laser and substrate.
- Polarization behaviour of all three Ag modes is the same from about 3.5 to 62 nm (Mondal 2025, p.4-5, Fig. 4);

- Layer number is better taken from optical contrast or AFM than from Raman shifts (Ye 2022, journal p.5).

# Writing the analysis notebook (Marimo)

The notebook is the deliverable: a researcher reruns it, sees how every number was produced, and checks every
citation. Start from the template; do not write the notebook from scratch.

## Steps

1. Copy `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/templates/raman_notebook.py` next to the data as `raman_analysis.py`.
2. Edit only the six cells marked `FILL`:
   1. **Sample, conditions, data**: `SAMPLE` (material, substrate, laser, temperature, the user's question, what
      you assumed), `SPECTRA` (label, file, series value or None), `SERIES` (name and unit of what varies),
      `BANDS` (search windows for the bands to track, from the material note), `MIN_SNR`.
   2. **Literature for this system**: `LIT_VALUES` (each reported number you compare with: quantity, band, value,
      uncertainty, source, figure or table locator, reference number) and `FIGURES` (the `image_path` from
      iopic-bond `view_figure`, caption, reference number).
   3. **Method notes**: each analysis choice that came from a paper, with its reference number.
   4. **Interpretation**: five to ten bullets, most likely reading first, then alternatives and the measurement
      that would decide. Each bullet is one claim, tagged `[measured]`, `[inferred]` or `[literature]`, with the
      number it rests on and its reference. Write numbers through `pos("label", "band")` inside the f-string so
      they come from the fit, never typed by hand.
   5. **Limits and questions** for the user (AFM, polarization, calibration lamp, laser power) and why.
   6. **References**: numbered, authors, year, title, journal or arXiv id, with a link
      (`https://arxiv.org/abs/<id>` or `https://doi.org/<doi>`).
3. Run `marimo export html raman_analysis.py -o raman_analysis.html`, then

   others, means the window or `MIN_SNR` needs adjusting.

   `marimo edit raman_analysis.py` to open the notebook.

correction, band positions across the series, and the literature table with figures. Change them only when the
analysis needs something they do not do (for example a polarization series); keep each change in its own cell.

## Citation rules

- Never cite from memory. A number with a citation comes from a figure you viewed, a table in a reference note, or
  a paper you ingested this session, with its figure or table locator.
- Cite the paper that reports the number, not a review that repeats it, unless the review is all you opened.
- When two papers disagree, show both values and say so.

- Every global name is defined in exactly one cell. Names local to a cell start with an underscore (`_fig`).
- A cell's arguments are the names it uses from other cells; its return tuple lists the names it defines.
  Never mutate another cell's object; build a new name.
- The last expression of a cell is what it shows (`mo.md(...)`, a figure, `mo.ui.table(rows)`).

Six spectra fall into three groups, and two of them (C and E) look degraded rather than thinner. This is a first pass: Bash was denied partway through, so the Marimo notebook and the windowed per-band fits were not produced.

**What the spectra share**

All six have the same quality-check result: no spikes, no flags, 1.2 cm⁻¹ point spacing, 50.8 to 430.8 cm⁻¹. There is no Si line in the window, so the wavenumber calibration cannot be checked. The three CrSBr Ag modes (Ag1 near 110, Ag2 near 243, Ag3 near 341 cm⁻¹) are present in all of them, as expected for normal incidence (Torres et al. 2022, arXiv:2212.01754, Eq. 2).

**How they differ**

Positions below are raw maxima, so each is good to about ±1 cm⁻¹. Only the Ag1 widths for A, B and D come from the series fit.

| Spectrum | Ag1 (cm⁻¹) | Ag2 (cm⁻¹) | Ag3 (cm⁻¹) | Character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 108.3, FWHM 9.1 | 241.3, weak | 341.6 | Red-shifted and broad Ag1, very weak Ag2 (about 0.07 of Ag3, versus about 0.4 in B) |
| B | 114.0, FWHM 3.6 | 245.0 | 342.8 | Sharp, lowest signal-to-noise of the sharp group |
| D | 113.3, FWHM 4.1 | 243.8 | 341.6 | Sharp |
| F | 112.1 | 242.6 | 340.4 | Sharp, strongest signal. The series fit pinned the Ag1 error at 0, so I used the raw maximum. |
| C | no sharp line, broad band centred near 100 | about 239, very weak | 340.4, broadened | Extra band near 302 |
| E | no sharp line, broad band centred near 100 | about 239, weak | 340.4, broadened | Extra band near 302 |

**Reading**

1. **A, B, D and F look like a thickness series.**
   - Torres Fig. 1h (read off the figure, about ±1 cm⁻¹, measured at 1.58 eV on SiO₂/Si) shows Ag1 rising from about 106.5 (1L) to 111 (2L), 112.5 (3L) and 114 (bulk).
   - Ag2 goes from about 240.8 (1L) to 244.5 (bulk), and Ag3 stays near 343.5.
   - By that trend, B and D match thick flakes (4L or more), F is intermediate, and A is the thinnest, around 1L to 2L.
   - Confidence is moderate for A, B and D, and low for F. A shifts of 1 to 2 cm⁻¹ is comparable to any calibration offset, and Torres used 1.58 eV rather than 532 nm. Ye et al. 2022 (ACS Nano 16, 11876) report the same direction of shift but advise taking layer number from optical contrast or AFM.
2. **C and E do not fit the thickness trend.**
   - Ag3 should not move with thickness, and in these two the Ag1 line has lost its sharp peak. The Ag1 region is replaced by a broad feature spanning roughly 80 to 105 cm⁻¹, with a fitted width of 65 to 68 cm⁻¹ versus 4 to 9 cm⁻¹ in A, B and D.
   - A band near 302 cm⁻¹ has appeared.
   - Torres report a surface-related D1 shoulder 5 to 10 cm⁻¹ below Ag1, plus broad defect features, after air, water or heat exposure. Degradation is my leading hypothesis for C and E, with low confidence.
   - I did not open Torres Fig. 2, the defect-mode figure, so I have not compared the line shapes.
3. **The 302 cm⁻¹ band is ambiguous.**
   - Pawbake et al. 2023 (PRB 107, 075421) assign a B2g mode at 301 cm⁻¹, but only with the sample tilted.
   - Torres report a resonant mode near 300 cm⁻¹ at 1.58 eV, and 532 nm is not resonant.
   - I would not assign it from this data alone.
4. **Absolute intensity is not a thickness measure.**
   - The Ag3 peak height above background ranges from about 1350 (C) to 17400 (F), and signal-to-noise from 90 to 364.
   - Thin-film interference changes the Ag2/Ag3 ratio in thick flakes (Mondal et al. 2025, arXiv:2410.22164), so use band positions and widths rather than intensity.
5. **All Ag3 maxima sit at 340.4 to 342.8 cm⁻¹**, against about 343 to 345 in the literature (Torres Fig. 1h; Pawbake 2023; Klein et al. 2023). That is a 1.2 cm⁻¹ grid step, so differences between spectra are not significant. The roughly 2 to 3 cm⁻¹ offset from the literature could be calibration. There is no Si line to check it, so I treat absolute positions with caution.

**What I could not do**

- I did not get the notebook (`raman_analysis.py`, HTML or PDF). The copy command was denied in this session's permission mode.
- I did not run the windowed per-band fits. The full-spectrum series fit merges weak and broad bands, so the C and E widths and the 302 cm⁻¹ band should be refit in their own windows.
- I did not run the library match or check the Valency literature beyond Torres Fig. 1.

If you allow shell commands again, I can finish the notebook and windowed fits. It would also help to know:
- the laser power, since 532 nm can damage thin CrSBr;
- how long and in what conditions C and E were exposed to air;
- the polarization angle relative to the a and b axes;
- AFM or optical-contrast thickness for each flake, which would settle A versus F.
